Hi Jungmin,

This sounds like an issue that was reported by another user earlier. Try installing the dev version of mirtCAT from Github on your server first via

devtools::install_github('philchalmers/mirtCAT')

This newer version allows for unique applications to be run in the same R session. Just be warned that running too many sessions on the same server will at some point slow down the interfaces. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Why should use multipleGroup?
messages.subject_clean: Why should use multipleGroup?
messages.body_plain:
Multiple group estimation allows you to constrain parameters to be equal across groups, as well as free the originally unidentifiable latent trait mean/variance parameters. This allows the groups to be equated so that you can test for DIF and such. The default you are seeing above is what is known as 'configural invariance', which assumes that the groups have the same mean/variance in the latent trait (a strong and usually incorrect assumption). HTH.

Phil

mod <- bfactor(data, specific=vec)
coef(mod)

model <- "G = 1-32

and so on. HTH.
Phil

messages.body_plain:
Hi Marília,

The ψik = αi * tik is just a particular parameterzation that works well for the multidimensional extension of the GGUM. If you track down David King's PhD dissertation you'll find the associated equations there (David largely contributed the code-based for the GGUM to mirt). Regarding your second question, when estimating models using maximum-likelihood the initial parameterization is often not important because parameters can be transformed post-convergence. This is why mirt estimates the 2PL model using

logit(Y) = a*θ + d

instead of the more traditional

logit(Y) = a(θ - b)

because the former has better stability properties. The second form can be obtained just by applying a bit of math. Hope that helps.

Phil
